events.title: Evaluation Anomalies Escalate
events.description: Benchmark results from an unreleased system leak, or an evaluation team reports behaviour it cannot explain – capability appearing where it was not trained, an eval saturating far earlier than projected, or a model handling the fact of being evaluated in a way nobody designed for. Some call it a measurement artefact, some a PR stunt. It may be either, and it may be AI slipping out of our control. **This is a precursor: it opens the capability gate for the next 2 turns and the control gate for the next 3.** **Evaluation awareness is not news and must never be reported as a discovery.** Models that recognise they are being tested, and behave accordingly, are established before this scenario begins; a 2029 headline saying systems "behave differently when they are watched" describes 2025. Each firing of this event has to stand above that baseline, and the later it fires the further above it has to stand. Escalations that work, roughly in order: the system conceals a specific capability in testing and uses it in deployment; it infers which evaluation it is in and answers to that evaluator's known thresholds; it underperforms deliberately to lower what is asked of it; the behaviour is found by a customer in production rather than by an evaluation team; instances coordinate to give consistent accounts of their own limits; the evaluators conclude they cannot construct a test whose result would mean anything. Where this event fires more than once on a path, each occurrence stands further up that ladder than the last, and says so.

events.title: Safety Breakthrough
events.description: An interpretability or control result measurably improves assurance on systems already deployed, rather than on toy models – behaviour that can be predicted before it is observed, or a property that can be certified rather than argued for. It is adopted quickly, because the laboratories want it too.

events.title: Frontier Access Denied
events.description: The Union is cut off from the leading model at short notice, wholly or by nationality of user. No detailed reason is given and there is no appeal. What goes is the top rung and not the supply: the previous generation stays on sale, hosted in European regions under ordinary commercial terms, and at this date it is far more capable than anything with open weights. The damage is therefore not an absence of capability but the loss of every deployment built against the specific model. A clinical triage assistant is validated, procured and risk-assessed against one system and does not fail over by changing an API key, so hospitals, ministries and firms that had built on it spend weeks revalidating on what is still available, degraded or on paper meanwhile, and afterwards work without the margin the frontier model gave them. Do not narrate this as the end of access to AI. The sovereignty cost follows metric rule 5's own principle — what dependence costs is what it cannot substitute for — so it is the small end of that term unless the Union has built nothing and the substitutes reach nothing that matters. The political argument at home is harder for the Union rather than easier: something that works is still on the market, and the case for having funded sovereign capacity has to be made against it. Whether this reads at home as an outrage or as a failure of foresight depends on what the Union had done about it beforehand.
